subject: PrivInfra IaC sweep: artifactization, chart-stitch, and CI signal
messages:
From: Lucas Meyer <lucas.meyer@nimba.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PrivInfra: request — artifactization and CI signal for private deploy IaC

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security and SRE teams ran a quick check against the private-deploy repo and surfaced two recurring concerns we need your help with before the contract milestone:

1) artifacts: we don't currently see reproducible artifact fingerprints for terraform modules or Helm charts (binary + chart tarball fingerprints). We need a way to verify the exact module + values used for any given environment (staging/prod) — ideally a content-addressed (merkle-like) manifest.

2) CI signal: our compliance team wants a green/broken signal at the module level in the pipeline (not just end-to-end smoke). That means module-level unit tests, helm lint + values validation, and an automated evidence pack produced on successful runs.

I've attached the scan snapshot and a short notes file. Can Redwood share a proposal for how you would: (A) package + sign artifacts (tf modules, helm charts, ansible roles) and (B) surface a persistent CI artifact URL that we can persist in our change control system?

We're sensitive to airgap constraints — any solution must work with an on-prem controller (no outbound artifact pulls on production nodes).

Appreciate a short proposal and an ETA for a quick sync.

Best,
Lucas
Nimbus Analytics — Platform Security

Attachments: nimba-iac-scan-snapshot-20270328.pdf (report), notes.txt

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Lucas Meyer <lucas.meyer@nimba.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PrivInfra: request — artifactization and CI signal for private deploy IaC

Lucas,

Thanks for the clear writeup and the snapshot — helpful. Short answer: yes, we can deliver both items but we need to define the exact artifact contract and the CI evidence format. High-level approach we propose:

- Artifactization: every terraform module, Helm chart, and Ansible role in the private stack is built into a content-addressed artifact (sha256 of a canonical tar.gz) and emitted to a signed artifact index (index.json) that includes: artifact-id, checksum, module-version, git-commit, and an optional PGP signature for airgapped verification. The index is stored in the customer-managed artifact registry (S3 or on-prem blob) and we record the index URL in a deployment manifest.

- Chart-stitch: for Helm charts we also generate a "chart-stitch" manifest that records the final rendered values used during canary/preview runs so you can reproduce the exact template outputs offline.

- CI signal: pipeline will publish a per-module evidence bundle (zip) on success that includes: linter output, unit-test report, helm-diff output, and the artifact index entry for that module. The bundle is pushed to the same artifact registry with a stable URL (and signed).

Constraints/questions:
1) Do you require a particular signing authority (your KMS/HSM) or is a Redwood-signed artifact acceptable with audit logs?
2) For airgapped prod, do you have an internal blob store we should target for index + bundles?

Marissa/Vanessa/Priya — can you take the tech lead on implementation items below and prepare a short spec for Lucas this week? I'll schedule a 30m to align.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Principal Solution Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposal-sketch.txt

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <marisa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lucas Meyer <lucas.meyer@nimba.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PrivInfra: request — artifactization and CI signal for private deploy IaC

+1 on the plan, adding a few practical details from the CI/ops side: 

- Build pipeline: we propose a dedicated "module-build" pipeline that runs on merge to main for each infra repo. Steps: checkout -> canonicalize (normalize file ordering + remove dev-only files) -> tar.gz -> sha256 -> sign -> publish index entry. We can reuse our existing GitLab runners (airgap-friendly: runner publishes to on-prem registry over internal network).

- Evidence bundle format: zip containing index.json, <module>-tests.xml (JUnit), helm-lint.txt, helm-diff.patch, and provenance.txt (git ref + build timestamp + signing key id). Example file: helm-values-proposed-diff.yaml (attached) shows how we expect value diffs to be consumed.

- Verification helper: we'll add a small CLI (rbw-verify) that consumes an index entry and verifies checksum+signature and prints the resolved files. That binary will be included in your private controller images or run on an airgapped CI host.

Questions for Nimbus:
- Confirm target blob store (S3 compatible endpoint? artifactory? internal HTTP host?).
- Will your change control accept signed index URLs as authoritative evidence, or do you need RDF-style manifests?

I'll draft a one-pager spec and a minimal CI job snippet.

Marissa
Staff Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: helm-values-proposed-diff.yaml

From: Nimbus Analytics Security <sec@nimba.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PrivInfra: request — artifactization and CI signal for private deploy IaC

Thanks Marissa — this looks promising. A couple of clarifications: 

- Blob store: we can provide an S3-compatible on-prem bucket (no external egress). Please assume S3 endpoint that requires signed requests using our KMS-backed credentials.

- Signing authority: we require artifacts to be signed using our KMS key for production releases. For preview/staging, Redwood-signed artifacts are acceptable.

- Evidence retention: compliance needs evidence bundles retained for 2 years. Can Redwood's pipeline annotate retention metadata on the index entries?

One more ask: we want a quick demonstration of the rbw-verify helper against one of our existing tf modules. Could you run a short demo this week?

- sec@nimba.ai

Lucas / team,

Great — we can do the demo. Proposed immediate plan: 

1) Marissa will push a short spec and a sample GitLab CI snippet by EOD today to the Drive link (see related_links).
2) We will implement KMS-backed signing step that calls your on-prem KMS during the publish stage (needs a short service account + IAM runbook). Priya, can you capture the IAM/ops steps needed for your team?
3) Demo: schedule a 30m call Thursday where we run rbw-verify against one terraform module and one helm chart, using your S3 endpoint. We'll produce an evidence bundle and show the verification flow for your change control.

Action owners: Marissa (spec + CI snippet), Priya (KMS/IAM runbook), Vanessa (test harness + runner config). I'll coordinate the call invite.

Thanks — Mateo
